_meta.indication: NATROBA (spinosad) Topical Suspension is a pediculicide indicated for the topical treatment of head lice infestations in patients four (4) years of age and older.

pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center, randomized, evaluator/investigator-blind, three-arm, active-controlled, parallel group study; households randomized 4:4:1 to NatrOVA without nit combing, NIX (permethrin 1%), or NatrOVA with nit combing
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects 6 months of age or older with active head lice (P. capitis) infestation
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of primary subjects in the randomized households who were lice free 14 days after the last treatment
pivotal_trials.n: 91 primary subjects randomized to NATROBA and 89 to permethrin 1%
pivotal_trials.result: 84.6% (77/91) of NATROBA subjects lice free vs 44.9% (40/89) permethrin 1%; treatment difference statistically significant (p<.001), treatment effect 40% (95% CI 27%, 52%)

pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center, randomized, evaluator/investigator-blind, three-arm, active-controlled, parallel group study; households randomized 4:4:1 to NatrOVA without nit combing, NIX (permethrin 1%), or NatrOVA with nit combing
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects 6 months of age or older with active head lice (P. capitis) infestation
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of primary subjects in the randomized households who were lice free 14 days after the last treatment
pivotal_trials.n: 83 primary subjects randomized to NATROBA and 84 to permethrin 1%
pivotal_trials.result: 86.7% (72/83) of NATROBA subjects lice free vs 42.9% (36/84) permethrin 1%; treatment difference statistically significant (p<.001), treatment effect 44% (95% CI 32%, 56%)

key_safety: Most common adverse events (>1%) were application site erythema (3% spinosad vs 7% permethrin) and ocular erythema (2% vs 3%); application site irritation occurred in 1% (vs 2%). Less common reactions (<1% but >0.1%) included application site dryness, exfoliation, alopecia, and dry skin.
target_moa: Spinosad is an insecticide/pediculicide that causes neuronal excitation in insects by altering the function of nicotinic and gamma butyric acid-gated ion channels, producing prolonged over-excitation; after hyperexcitation, lice become paralyzed and die.
modality: Small molecule (spinosad, a fermentation-derived insecticide composed of spinosyns A and D), new molecular entity

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee was convened; NDA 22-408 was not presented to the Dermatology and Ophthalmology Drugs Advisory Committee because systemic exposure was below the level of detection and no safety signals or novel issues were identified.

description.text: Expanded indication to include patients 6 months of age and older with head lice infestation

citations.quote: This “Prior Approval” supplemental new drug application provides for the modification of the Natroba (spinosad) Topical Suspension, 0.9% indication to include patients 6 months of age and older with head lice infestation.

description.text: Added new indication for topical treatment of scabies infestations in adult and pediatric patients 4 years of age and older

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for a new indication for the topical treatment of scabies infestations in adult and pediatric patients 4 years of age and older.

basis.text: The application was granted a standard review (Priority Designation: Standard).

citations.quote: NDA 022408 was originally submitted on January 21, 2009, received on January 22, 2009, and granted a standard review.

summary.text: NATROBA (spinosad), a new molecular entity, was submitted as a 505(b)(1) NDA and granted standard review; it was not referred to an advisory committee. The original NDA received a Complete Response Letter on November 18, 2009 (over whether benzyl alcohol was a second active ingredient), and was approved following the applicant's complete response, with a deferred PREA pediatric PK/safety study as a postmarketing requirement.

citations.quote: The applicant, ParaPro Pharmaceuticals, submitted a 505(b)(1) application for Tradename (spinosad) Suspension, 0.9%.
NDA 022408 was originally submitted on January 21, 2009, received on January 22, 2009, and granted a standard review.
A Complete Response Letter was issued November 18, 2009.

requirement.text: Deferred pediatric study under PREA (#1711): a pharmacokinetic and safety study in pediatric patients ages 6 months to 4 years with active head lice infestation, conducted under maximum use conditions with a minimum of 24 evaluable patients undergoing PK sampling and local/systemic safety assessments.

citations.quote: 1711 A pharmacokinetic and safety study in pediatric patients ages 6 months to 4 years of age with active head lice infestation. This study should be conducted under maximum use conditions and include a minimum of 24 evaluable patients who will undergo pharmacokinetic sampling and assessments of local and systemic safety at appropriate time points.
A Complete Response Letter was issued November 18, 2009.

basis.text: FDA concluded the product appeared to contain two active ingredients (spinosad and benzyl alcohol), because a product containing 5% benzyl alcohol had recently been approved as an active ingredient for head lice; the applicant was asked to provide information to support benzyl alcohol as an inactive ingredient (plus PK and CMC items).

citations.quote: However, we have recently approved a product containing benzyl alcohol (present at 5%) as an active ingredient for the treatment of head lice. This would indicate that your product contains two active ingredients: spinosad and benzyl alcohol (b) (4).
